findings.title: Owner's saved sales are deleted with dummy data — saving a seeded date leaves it flagged as dummy
findings.surface: Input Harian; Settings > Hapus Semua Dummy; POST /api/daily-input; DELETE /api/dummy
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: an owner who edits and successfully syncs any seeded dummy day still has their entire edited day classified as dummy. Confirming Hapus Semua Dummy permanently deletes those real sales, cup and SPG values despite the safety assurance; the user has no in-app recovery.
findings.evidence: backend/server.py:222-225 sets is_dummy to false only in $setOnInsert, so updating an existing dummy day retains true; :289-292 deletes all documents with is_dummy true. Fresh startup generates dummy days at :356-358, and SettingsTab.jsx:102,146-148 promises the user's real data remains safe.
findings.expected: R-047: "removes only the dummy rows while days the owner saved himself still show their values afterwards"; R-048: "real owner-saved rows ... unchanged and still readable".
reproduction_steps: Open today's pre-seeded data in Input Harian and replace a stand's omset with the real amount.
Wait for Tersinkronisasi Server or press Simpan Sekarang.
Open Settings, choose Hapus Semua Dummy, and confirm.
Return to today: the saved real values were deleted with the dummy day.

findings.title: Recent sales can be overwritten by an older autosave — concurrent full-day writes have no ordering or conflict guard
findings.surface: Input Harian; POST /api/daily-input
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: if an earlier autosave is delayed while the user edits again and a later save reaches the database first, the older request can overwrite the later day's entire payload. The newer response may already have marked the draft synced, so a reload shows stale sales and a WA report or Excel can omit the latest work.
findings.evidence: useDaily.js:37-41 posts each snapshot without awaiting or serializing earlier syncs; :43-45 only protects the local clean marker. server.py:222-225 unconditionally replaces the complete entries object with each arriving request, without a version or compare-and-set.
findings.expected: R-057: "Two saves arriving together ... holding the later submitted values"; R-016: drafts clear only once the relevant server save is confirmed.
reproduction_steps: Enter a value for a stand and pause until autosave begins on a slow connection.
Edit the value again and trigger another save before the first finishes.
Let the newer request complete before the older one.
Reload the day and compare with the last value entered.

findings.title: A late day load erases values typed while loading — the GET response replaces new local edits
findings.surface: Input Harian date change and reopening a draft
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: on a slow date read, a user can edit a cached day before its GET returns. The response replaces the edit and marks the draft clean; the effect may then save the old values. This loses newly entered sales or staff information without warning.
findings.evidence: useDaily.js:59-64 renders cached entries and starts GET; :65-72 unconditionally setEntries(data.entries) and writeDraft(..., false) when the initially captured draft was clean. StandCard.jsx:31-36,45-50,58-65 leaves all fields editable while the request runs; InputTab.jsx:38 only hides cards when entries are empty.
findings.expected: R-015: "Every keystroke ... writes the whole selected date's payload"; R-016: restore unsynced data without losing newer edits.
reproduction_steps: Open a previously cached date while its network request is slow.
Immediately edit an existing stand before the loading request finishes.
Allow the GET to finish and inspect the field and local draft.

findings.title: Long pivot ranges silently omit days and understate totals — date generation stops after 93 days
findings.surface: Pivot & Export date range and three Excel sheets
findings.observed: Business logic and calculations: an owner choosing a range longer than 93 days sees and exports totals for only the first 93 days while the date controls and filename still identify the complete requested range. Sales and cup totals are materially understated, with no indication that later dates were discarded.
findings.evidence: format.js:32 stops dateRange once out.length reaches 93, without error; PivotTab.jsx:68-77 builds all matrices and exports using these dates but names the workbook with the full requested start and end. pivot.js:12-19 and :29-36 sum only the supplied dates.
findings.expected: R-058: "Each pivot cell equals the sum ... across the inclusive range"; R-059: a range "always includes both its start and end dates and no day outside them".
reproduction_steps: Save values at both the start and the end of a range exceeding 93 days.
Select the full range in Pivot & Export.
Inspect the last date columns and totals, then export the Excel workbook.

findings.title: Dummy generation and clearing can erase unsynced real drafts — Settings removes local date drafts indiscriminately
findings.surface: Settings > Buat 7 Hari / Hapus Semua Dummy
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: when an owner has an unsynced local edit on a dummy date and then generates or clears dummy data after connectivity returns, Settings deletes the only local copy without checking dirty state. The onDataChanged reload replaces it with regenerated data or an empty day. Sales and staff edits that never reached the server are lost.
findings.evidence: SettingsTab.jsx:82 removes amk_draft for every date last reported as dummy after deletion; :91 removes the same keys following generation. useDaily.js:13-14 stores both dirty real edits and clean cached values under those keys; server.py:259-260 and :277-279 regenerates days still flagged dummy.
findings.expected: R-016: "automatically restore un-synced data"; R-047: clearing dummy leaves owner-saved data intact; R-051: "nothing typed is lost".
reproduction_steps: Edit a dummy day while offline so the draft is unsynced.
Reconnect and, before that draft finishes saving, open Settings and clear or regenerate dummy data.
Return to the day and inspect the entered values.

findings.title: Switching or deleting a stand removes its historical sales from reports — reports rely on mutable current master records
findings.surface: Settings > Stand; WA Generator; Pivot & Export
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: deleting a stand that has daily history leaves its entries in the store but makes its past omset, cups and SPG disappear from pivot, Excel and WA totals; deactivating a stand also hides its historical SPG. The owner can no longer reconcile reported history and cannot restore the deleted stand with its original id through Settings.
findings.evidence: SettingsTab.jsx:123-130 exposes delete; server.py:194-197 deletes the stand without checking daily_inputs. pivot.js:9-20 builds all historical omset rows and totals only from current stands and :43 excludes every inactive stand from SPG. wa.js:6-14 and :36-40 also traverse only current stand records.
findings.expected: R-044: "a deactivated stand drops out of the active input list while its historical saved values remain readable"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Deleting a parent handles its children (cascade, block or reassign)".
reproduction_steps: Save sales, cups and SPG for a stand on an earlier date.
In Settings deactivate the stand and inspect the historical SPG matrix.
Delete the same stand and reopen the historical WA and pivot reports; the stand and its values are absent.

findings.title: A manual save during initial loading can erase the whole day — the save button sends empty entries before the read completes
findings.surface: Input Harian > Simpan Sekarang
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: on a slow connection, the owner can press Simpan Sekarang while an uncached existing day is loading. The empty payload can replace all previously saved stand values; success is reported as a normal save and there is no recovery in the app.
findings.evidence: useDaily.js:59-64 initializes entries to {} for an uncached date and starts GET; InputTab.jsx:38-41 shows a loading indicator, but :49 disables Save only when status === syncing. saveNow at useDaily.js:107-110 sends latest.current.entries; server.py:222-225 replaces the whole stored entries object.
findings.expected: R-020: saved data reads back unchanged and a save upserts stand values; checklist, UI state: "loading, disabled ... states" prevent premature actions.
reproduction_steps: Open an existing day on a device without a local cached draft, with a slow network.
While Memuat data is displayed press Simpan Sekarang.
Reload that date after the save completes.

findings.title: Pivot and Excel can combine the chosen dates with another range's data — overlapping fetches are applied without checking their range
findings.surface: Pivot & Export date controls, matrix and Excel download
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: rapidly changing the pivot dates on a slow network permits an older request to finish last. The visible and exported matrices then use the latest date labels but old-range documents, producing missing or incorrect figures without warning.
findings.evidence: PivotTab.jsx:51-56 starts a GET for each start/end state and calls setDocs(data) on every completion; :64-66 reruns it on each change with no cancellation or request identity. :68-71 builds columns from current start/end against whichever docs last completed; :74-79 exports that result.
findings.expected: R-058: "Each pivot cell equals the sum ... across the inclusive range"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Search-as-you-type applies only the latest response".
reproduction_steps: Open Pivot & Export on a slow connection.
Change the date range twice in quick succession so both requests overlap.
Let the older range's request complete last, then inspect and export the current range.

findings.title: Saving one stand removes the day's other saved stands — the API replaces the whole entries map instead of upserting stands
findings.surface: POST /api/daily-input; Input Harian and reports
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: an authenticated client that saves just one stand for a date overwrites every other stand on that date, rather than updating that stand. On shared or stale-device workflows this destroys other entries and alters WA and pivot totals, with no historical recovery.
findings.evidence: DailyIn at server.py:207-209 accepts a map of entries, but save_daily at :220-225 sets the day's entire entries map to exactly that submitted map, replacing all unmentioned stands; GET at :212-215 reads that same document.
findings.expected: R-020: "upserts one row per stand and date, so a second save for the same stand and date replaces the numbers instead of duplicating them"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "a partial update leaves the fields the form did not show as they were".
reproduction_steps: Save two stands for one date using POST /api/daily-input.
Send a second save for that date containing only one of those stands.
Read the date again: the other stand is gone.

findings.title: Edits on a previous day remain unsynced after switching dates or reconnecting — only the currently selected draft is retried
findings.surface: Input Harian date selector and offline autosync
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: a user who edits a day and switches dates before the debounce, or reconnects on a different day, leaves the original date dirty indefinitely. It is stored only on that phone and will be missing from pivot and WA on another device until the user discovers and reopens that date.
findings.evidence: useDaily.js:56 cancels the date's debounce when date changes; :67-68 syncs a dirty draft only when that date is loaded, and :91-93 syncs only latest.current.date when online. There is no queue or scan for other dirty draft keys.
findings.expected: R-052: "on reconnect they sync and read back from the server for that same date"; R-017: "After the user stops typing ... sends a background POST".
reproduction_steps: Edit day A while offline or switch to day B immediately after typing.
Reconnect or stay online with day B selected.
Open Pivot & Export for day A or sign in on another device; day A's edit has not synced.
Return to day A to trigger its save.

findings.title: Signed-out owner's sales remain exposed on the device — logout keeps cached records and offline authentication trusts any token
findings.surface: Sign-out; offline login gate; local sales cache
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: logout leaves cached stand information and sales on a shared device, and if a token is present while authentication cannot reach the server, the app accepts it without validating it and displays cached data. A later device user with browser storage access can read the previous owner's sales after sign-out.
findings.evidence: AuthContext.js:15-17 treats any non-401 failure of /auth/me as an authenticated offline user; :29-31 logout removes only the token. App.js:18-23 and useDaily.js:5-14 persist master and daily entries in localStorage and do not clear them on logout.
findings.expected: R-067: "sign-out ... discards the stored token ... and the browser back button does not reveal stand, pivot or WA data"; checklist, Auth, sessions and access control: "Signing out clears the previous user's data from the client store, caches and localStorage".
reproduction_steps: Sign in, open a day's data and sign out.
Inspect the app's browser local storage: master data and daily draft/cache remain.
With the network unavailable and any stale token present, reopen the app and observe that cached screens are accessible without server validation.

findings.title: A signed-out session can still read and change the owner's records — bearer tokens are never revoked
findings.surface: Settings > Keluar; all protected API routes
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: a previously captured or copied session token continues to access and modify all sales and master data until it expires, even after the owner presses Keluar. The owner cannot terminate an exposed session from the app.
findings.evidence: AuthContext.js:29-31 removes the browser copy only. server.py:60-63 issues a seven-day JWT and :66-79 validates only its signature, expiry and user existence; the API route list has no logout or revocation endpoint.
findings.expected: R-068: "the sign-out call itself completes without leaving the session usable"; checklist, Auth, sessions and access control: "a revoked session ... stops working on its next request".
reproduction_steps: Sign in and retain the issued session token in a separate client.
Press Keluar in Settings.
Use the retained token against a protected data route before its expiry.

findings.title: An owner who forgets the password cannot regain access — no password recovery flow exists
findings.surface: Login and account recovery
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: if the single owner forgets the password, there is no self-service recovery route and no way to access sales or enter new days through the application. Recovery requires an operator to change server credentials or database state.
findings.evidence: Login.jsx:26-50 contains only email, password and Masuk; server.py:87-109 implements login and me, and the full route index has no password-recovery or reset route or mail delivery.
findings.expected: checklist, Auth, sessions and access control: "Forgot-password exists wherever accounts exist: a request form, an email actually sent, a reset link ... single-use and expires".
reproduction_steps: Open the login screen without the owner password.
Look for a password recovery option.

findings.title: The application cannot run on the requested PHP/Laravel SQL stack — it is implemented in FastAPI, MongoDB and React
findings.surface: Application architecture and deployment
findings.observed: Build, deployment and environment: the delivered application is Python/FastAPI, MongoDB and React rather than the specifically requested PHP/Laravel, SQL and Alpine stack. An owner deploying or maintaining on the requested PHP 8.5 and SQLite/MySQL environment cannot run this application without provisioning an entirely different stack.
findings.evidence: server.py:19-21 imports FastAPI and Motor, :25-26 connects to MongoDB, and :39-40 defines FastAPI routes. package.json:48-54 uses React. No Laravel/PHP application, SQLite/MySQL schema or Alpine.js entry point appears in the source inventory.
findings.expected: R-082: "Laravel 11 with SQLite/MySQL, Tailwind CSS, Alpine.js and SheetJS"; R-083: "runs on PHP 8.5".
reproduction_steps: Attempt to deploy the delivered app on a PHP 8.5 Laravel 11 host with SQLite/MySQL.
Inspect the backend and frontend manifests and startup entry points.

findings.title: Historical cup quantities disappear from reports when an item is deactivated or deleted — reports use only current active items
findings.surface: Settings > Item Cup; WA Generator; Percup pivot and Excel
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: after the owner deactivates or deletes a cup item, previously recorded cup quantities disappear from historical pivot and Excel; deactivating a standard WA item also makes old WA reports print its saved counts as blank. Deleting it prevents restoring the original item id, so historical quantities cannot be recovered from the UI.
findings.evidence: App.js:46 filters allItems to active items and passes only those to WA and Pivot at :77-78. pivot.js:32-36 creates rows and totals only from passed items; wa.js:20-31 locates Ck, Cb and Csdng in that same active list. server.py:171-174 deletes an item without handling historical cups.
findings.expected: R-044: historical saved values remain readable; R-058: pivot sums stored values; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Deleting a parent handles its children".
reproduction_steps: Enter and save 12oz quantities for a past day.
Deactivate 12oz in Settings and reopen that day's WA and Percup matrix.
Delete 12oz and try to recover the historical counts through the UI.

findings.title: An offline owner cannot reliably reopen the saved draft — no application shell or assets are cached for offline use
findings.surface: Offline reload and reopening Input Harian
findings.observed: Build, deployment and environment: localStorage preserves draft data but does not serve the application's HTML and JavaScript. Without an offline-capable app shell, an owner who reloads or reopens while disconnected cannot reliably open the form to restore or continue a draft; behavior depends on incidental browser cache.
findings.evidence: index.js:16-23 only mounts React and never registers a service worker; public/index.html:24-30 loads the normal online application shell. The source inventory contains no service-worker registration, offline manifest or offline asset caching implementation.
findings.expected: R-052: "With the network disabled, values typed into a date survive a page reload from the local draft"; request: "If the browser refreshes, loses connection, or closes accidentally, automatically restore un-synced data ... upon reopening".
reproduction_steps: Sign in and create a local draft while online.
Disable connectivity and close or reload the app after the browser has evicted or revalidated the network assets.
Attempt to reopen Input Harian and restore the draft.

findings.title: A failed master-data request leaves no input cards and falsely says all stands are filled — the error is swallowed
findings.surface: Input Harian and useMaster loading state
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: on a first session when the master-data request fails, the owner is shown zero stands and a misleading all-filled message instead of an error or retry. They cannot enter sales and may believe there is nothing to do.
findings.evidence: useMaster in App.js:21-25 initializes to empty arrays without a cache and :33-35 swallows every /master error. :53-61 derives all stand cards from those arrays; InputTab.jsx:42-43 then says all stands in the filter are filled.
findings.expected: R-065: "a screen whose data request fails shows an error message in Bahasa Indonesia instead of a blank page"; R-009: Semua shows the 28 active stands.
reproduction_steps: Sign in on a browser without a cached master list while GET /api/master fails.
Open Input Harian and inspect the cards, counts and empty-state message.

findings.title: Reopening an older offline draft overwrites newer server sales — restoration never compares draft and server versions
findings.surface: Offline draft restoration across devices; POST /api/daily-input
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: when an old offline draft is reopened after newer sales for the same day were saved on another device, the hook immediately posts the stale complete draft over the newer server record. This destroys the newer sales and staff entries without a warning or conflict choice.
findings.evidence: useDaily.js:59-60 reads savedAt but :67-71 tests only draft.dirty, unconditionally syncing the local draft when dirty and otherwise taking the server result. server.py:215 returns updated_at and :221-225 writes it, but no comparison or conflict resolution uses it.
findings.expected: R-016 notes: "Restore must prefer the newer of local draft and server row"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Two tabs or two users editing one record keep both users' intent or refuse one".
reproduction_steps: Create an unsynced draft for a day on device A.
On device B save newer values for that day.
Reconnect and open the day on device A; inspect the day on device B after A's automatic sync.

findings.title: A failed day read can erase previously saved stands — blank cards remain editable and save replaces the entire day
findings.surface: Input Harian day load failure and save
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: if a date read fails but a subsequent POST succeeds, the owner sees an apparently blank day, enters one stand and saves; the server replaces the existing full day with only the new entry. The other previously saved stands are lost with no readable error or recovery.
findings.evidence: useDaily.js:59-61 initializes an uncached day to empty; :63-75 catches a failed GET only by setting status draft; :76 ends loading. InputTab.jsx:38-46 then renders editable empty cards, and server.py:222-225 replaces existing entries on save.
findings.expected: R-019: "read endpoint ... returns ... stored ... values"; R-065: request failures show an Indonesian error rather than a blank page; R-020: no previously saved data lost on save.
reproduction_steps: On a fresh device select a date with existing sales while its GET fails.
After loading ends, enter one stand and press Simpan Sekarang once POST requests work.
Reload the day and inspect the previously saved stands.

findings.title: Failed pivot loads can produce misleading reports for the new range — old documents remain paired with new date labels
findings.surface: Pivot & Export range fetch failure and Excel export
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: when a date-range request fails, the displayed dates switch to the new range but the calculation silently reuses the previous range's documents. Export becomes enabled and can create a plausible zero or partial workbook for a range whose data was never fetched, causing misleading sales totals.
findings.evidence: PivotTab.jsx:55-56 replaces docs only on success; :57-60 displays a toast but retains old docs. :68-71 immediately builds matrices using the newly edited dates and retained docs, and :99 enables export when loading ends even after failure.
findings.expected: R-058: "Each pivot cell equals the sum of the stored daily values ... across the inclusive range"; checklist, UI state: "a visible error when its request fails" and exports reflect current data.
reproduction_steps: Load a populated range in Pivot & Export.
Change to another range while GET /daily-inputs fails.
After the toast disappears, inspect the matrix and export the workbook.

findings.title: Generating dummy data can overwrite a concurrently saved real day — the existing-data check and replacement are not atomic
findings.surface: Settings > Buat 7 Hari; POST /api/dummy/generate and /api/daily-input
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: when dummy generation races with a real save for an initially empty date, the generator can replace the newly saved day with random values and mark it dummy. The real sales and staff data are lost even though the save succeeded; clearing dummy can then remove the replacement too.
findings.evidence: generate_dummy reads each date's is_dummy status at server.py:259-260, then unconditionally updates by date and sets entries/is_dummy at :277-279. A concurrent save_daily at :218-225 can write real entries after the check but before that update; no transaction or conditional is_dummy filter prevents the replacement.
findings.expected: R-046: "running it again does not corrupt or duplicate real owner-saved rows"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Two tabs or two users editing one record keep both users' intent or refuse one".
reproduction_steps: Use two signed-in tabs on a previously empty date within the last seven days.
Start Buat 7 Hari in one tab while saving real stand data for that date in the other.
If the real save lands between the generator's read and update, reload the date.

findings.title: Deactivated stands still appear in WhatsApp reports and totals — the generator ignores the active-input flag
findings.surface: Settings > Stand active toggle; WA Generator
findings.observed: Business logic and calculations: after the owner switches an ordinary stand off in Settings, its card disappears but its WA line and any recorded sales still appear in the report. The output therefore includes a stand the operator deliberately removed; reactivating is not needed to see it.
findings.evidence: MasterDialogs.jsx:95 saves is_active_input; wa.js:37 selects stands solely by wa_group and wa.js:6-14 totals every matching category regardless of is_active_input. The seeded TRANS exception is also is_active_input false (server.py:348).
findings.expected: R-055: "Deactivating a stand ... removes its card from Input Harian and its line from the WA preview after reload" while R-032 keeps the special TRANS line.
reproduction_steps: Edit WTC in Settings and turn off Tampil di Input Harian.
Open WA Generator and inspect the first group and Total AMK.
Reactivate WTC to restore the input card.

findings.title: Saved zero-sales or cup-only stands are marked incomplete — the filled test checks only positive omset
findings.surface: Input Harian cards, Terisi summary and Belum Diisi filter
findings.observed: Business logic and calculations: a saved stand with an explicit zero omset, or with only cups or staff recorded, remains unchecked and listed as Belum Diisi. Its owner sees the wrong completion count and cannot reliably tell which stands still need entry.
findings.evidence: App.js:54 defines isEmpty as !(Number(daily.entries[s.id]?.omset) > 0), InputTab.jsx:18 uses the same positive-omset test for Terisi, and StandCard.jsx:8 uses it for the checkmark. server.py:214-215 returns the saved entries keyed by stand.
findings.expected: R-049: "a stand counts as filled once it has a saved row for the date, whatever the values; a stand with an all-zero row counts as filled".
reproduction_steps: On an empty day enter staff or cup values for a stand with no omset, then save.
Select Belum Diisi and inspect the stand and Terisi count.
Alternatively save a zero-valued entry and reload.

findings.title: WhatsApp reports show large cup counts without required thousand separators — cup values bypass the number formatter
findings.surface: WA Generator preview and Copy ke WhatsApp
findings.observed: Files, media and generated artifacts: a saved cup quantity of 1173 is copied into individual WA stand lines as 1173 rather than 1.173, even though the footer formats the same quantity. The owner must manually correct the report.
findings.evidence: wa.js:22-25 converts positive cup counts with String(v), while :28 formats omset with fmt and :45 formats the aggregate Ck total with fmt. The cup string is inserted in all stand lines at :29-31.
findings.expected: R-028: "Every number in the WA preview uses dot thousand separators"; request: "Format numbers with dot thousand separators".
reproduction_steps: Enter 1173 in a stand's 12oz or 22oz input.
Open WA Generator and inspect the corresponding cup count.
Copy the report and compare the copied number with 1.173.

findings.title: Invalid pivot dates discard the displayed matrix and allow an empty export — columns follow unvalidated inputs
findings.surface: Pivot & Export date selectors and Export Excel
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: when the owner selects a start later than the end, the old matrix loses all date columns and export still produces a workbook for the invalid range rather than preserving the last valid result. The owner must reconstruct the previous range.
findings.evidence: PivotTab.jsx:52 only returns a toast when start > end; :68 simultaneously turns dates into [] for that invalid pair and :69-72 rebuild the matrix. :74-79 exports those matrices using the invalid dates.
findings.expected: R-092: "a start date later than the end date is refused ... and the previously rendered matrices stay on screen".
reproduction_steps: Open a populated pivot range.
Set Dari later than Sampai.
Observe the matrix and press Export Excel.

findings.title: Failed autosaves are not explained or retried after server recovery — errors only change the draft pill
findings.surface: Input Harian background autosave
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: a server-side save error while the device remains online silently leaves the draft pill active and does not schedule any retry; no message explains the failure. Even after the server recovers, the owner must notice the pill and manually retry or edit again.
findings.evidence: useDaily.js:48-50 catches save failure and only sets status draft; :75 catches a GET failure likewise; :90-97 retries solely on an online event. InputTab.jsx:20-24 shows a toast only for a manually initiated save, not autosave.
findings.expected: R-051: "When the autosave request fails (offline or server error) ... a visible message says the data is not yet on the server"; checklist, UI state: failures must offer retry and end in a message.
reproduction_steps: Enter a value while the API is returning a server error but the phone remains connected.
Wait for the 1.5-second autosave and then restore the server.
Observe that no error message or automatic retry occurs.

findings.title: Invalid dates and negative cup quantities can be saved into the sales ledger — the server validates only omset and date shape
findings.surface: POST /api/daily-input; WA and Percup totals
findings.observed: Business logic and calculations: a direct authenticated save can persist negative cup counts, nonexistent stand/item IDs and impossible date strings. Negative quantities feed Percup sums and AMKopi totals, causing misleading business reports and unfindable entries.
findings.evidence: server.py:202 enforces ge=0 only for omset; :203 declares cups as Dict[str, int] with no nonnegative constraint and :208 validates only a date-shaped regex. :220-225 stores all supplied values without checking item or stand ids or calendar validity.
findings.expected: R-050: "no non-numeric or negative value is ever saved or included in a total"; checklist, Business logic and calculations: "server enforces every rule the UI shows" and dates compare as dates.
reproduction_steps: Call POST /api/daily-input as the owner with a negative cup quantity for a real item.
Read the day and open its Percup matrix.
Submit a date with the correct YYYY-MM-DD shape but impossible month/day and observe it is accepted.

findings.title: Duplicate or blank cup items make reports ambiguous — names, WA codes and order fields lack validation and uniqueness
findings.surface: Settings > Tambah Item; items API
findings.observed: Business logic and calculations: Settings accepts whitespace-only item names, negative sort positions and duplicate cup names or WA codes. Duplicated Ck codes make the WA generator select one item arbitrarily, hiding the other's cup count and making reports ambiguous.
findings.evidence: ItemIn.name only has min_length=1 at server.py:114 so whitespace passes; sort_order is unconstrained at :116. POST /items at :155-158 inserts without checking name or code; INDEXES :31-37 makes only generated ids unique. wa.js:4,20 uses the first active item with a WA code.
findings.expected: checklist, Business logic and calculations: "text is trimmed and non-empty" and counts/order have bounds; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "What must be unique is unique in the store through a unique index".
reproduction_steps: In Settings add an item whose name contains only spaces.
Give two items the same Ck code or the same name, or enter a negative ordering value.
Open Input Harian and WA Generator to inspect the labels and counts.

findings.title: Double-tapping a master-data save creates duplicate stands or items — the dialog ignores the pending request
findings.surface: Settings > Tambah Stand / Tambah Item dialogs
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: double-tapping Simpan during a slow create sends duplicate master records. The duplicates appear as extra stands or items in cards, WhatsApp and pivot, requiring manual cleanup and risking inaccurate reports.
findings.evidence: MasterDialogs.jsx:25-30 always enables the submit button and invokes onSubmit on each submission; SettingsTab.jsx:47-55 tracks busy but does not pass it into either dialog, and :59-73 issues a new POST for each create. server.py:155-158,177-180 always inserts a fresh id.
findings.expected: checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: "A submit button disables while its request is pending, so a double click creates one record".
reproduction_steps: Open Settings > Tambah Stand or Tambah Item.
Fill the form and double-tap Simpan before the first request returns.
Inspect the newly created master list.

findings.title: Reloads and direct links open Input Harian instead of the requested tab — navigation is only transient React state
findings.surface: Bottom navigation, browser reload and deep links
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: refreshing WA, Pivot or Settings always returns to Input Harian, and direct links such as /pivot or /settings do not select their named screen. Unknown paths likewise render Input Harian rather than a not-found state; users lose navigation context.
findings.evidence: App.js:40 initializes tab to input unconditionally and :76-81 switches only on local state; BottomNav.jsx:20 calls setTab without changing URL. index.js:16-23 mounts App without any router.
findings.expected: R-064: "a browser reload returns the user to the tab they were on"; R-069: after sign-in the user reaches the requested screen; checklist, UI state: "An unknown route shows a not-found page".
reproduction_steps: Open Pivot & Export and refresh the browser.
Open /settings directly and sign in if prompted.
Open an unknown path and observe the result.

findings.title: Percup and its workbook repeat stands instead of adding item columns — matrix construction makes every item a separate row
findings.surface: Pivot & Export > Percup; Excel Percup sheet
findings.observed: Files, media and generated artifacts: the Percup matrix and Excel repeat each stand once for every item instead of exposing one stand row with an item column for each configured cup. With added items the operator gets a different workbook structure than requested and cannot compare the item columns as specified.
findings.evidence: pivot.js:27 sets header to Stand, Item, dates and Total; :32-33 emits one row for every stand/item combination; exportXlsx at :52-57 writes that identical matrix to the Percup sheet.
findings.expected: R-041: "each stand appears once per measure"; R-090: adding an item adds "a matching column to the Percup matrix and a matching column to the exported sheet".
reproduction_steps: Open the Percup pivot with the default three items.
Observe that each stand occupies three rows and no cup-item columns exist.
Add an item and export Excel; inspect the Percup sheet.

findings.title: Older staff names disappear from autocomplete — the suggestion endpoint scans only the latest 120 days
findings.surface: Input Harian SPG datalist; GET /api/spg-names
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: once the owner has more than 120 daily records, a staff name used only in older history is no longer suggested, despite remaining saved. The owner has to retype it or search historical data manually.
findings.evidence: GET /spg-names at server.py:238 reads only the 120 most recent date documents, then gathers names from those documents at :240-243. App.js:49-51 loads that response for the datalist.
findings.expected: R-014: "The API exposes the distinct SPG names previously saved"; R-013: suggestions include previously entered SPG names.
reproduction_steps: Save an SPG name on an early day.
Save daily records on at least 120 later days without that name.
Open a card's SPG field and look for the earlier name in suggestions.

findings.title: Errors appear in English and technical wording — network and validation messages are passed through untranslated
findings.surface: Login, Pivot and Settings error messages; API validation responses
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: a network failure or invalid backend payload produces raw English transport or Pydantic validation text in the login, pivot or settings error. The owner receives technical wording rather than an actionable Indonesian message.
findings.evidence: api.js:26 returns raw e.message for network errors and :28 returns FastAPI validation msg values unaltered. server.py uses the default FastAPI validation handling with no exception handler or translation, and Login.jsx:20, PivotTab.jsx:58, SettingsTab.jsx:53 render errMsg to the user.
findings.expected: R-004: "Every visible ... error message ... is in Bahasa Indonesia"; R-005: "API responses ... return Bahasa Indonesia messages alongside a machine-readable code".
reproduction_steps: Attempt sign-in with the network unavailable, or submit an invalid Settings value that reaches backend validation.
Read the displayed error message.

findings.title: The owner can leave with unsynced sales without warning — no unsaved-draft navigation guard is registered
findings.surface: Input Harian unsynced navigation and page close
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: when the owner closes the page while a draft remains local, there is no warning that sales have not reached the server. The draft can be recovered on the same device but will not be available elsewhere unless later reopened and synced.
findings.evidence: useDaily.js tracks status and dirty drafts at :30-34 and :82-87, but its only window listener at :90-97 is online; there is no beforeunload or equivalent navigation guard in the frontend source.
findings.expected: R-089: "Leaving or closing the page while a draft is still unsynced triggers a visible warning or the browser's unsaved-changes prompt".
reproduction_steps: Edit a day offline or during a failed save.
Close or navigate away while the status is Draft Lokal.
Observe that there is no unsynced-work warning.

findings.title: Autosave continues after sign-out — the pending timer is not cleared when the form unmounts
findings.surface: Input Harian autosave and Settings > Keluar
findings.observed: Performance and resource leaks: when the owner signs out within 1.5 seconds of an edit, the unmounted form's timer still fires a POST after sign-out. If the owner signs back in before it fires, that stale request uses the newly stored token and may write the old snapshot over current work.
findings.evidence: useDaily.js:82-87 starts a debounce timer and its date effect cleanup at :77-79 only marks the fetch canceled; it does not clear timer.current on Shell unmount. AuthContext.js:29-31 unmounts Shell on logout.
findings.expected: R-079: "Leaving a tab cancels its pending autosave timer ... only one save per edit reaches the server"; R-067: sign-out "sends no further authenticated requests".
reproduction_steps: Edit a field and immediately sign out before the debounce expires.
Observe the pending POST after sign-out, or sign in again immediately before it fires.

findings.title: Long-range API responses silently omit later sales — the daily-data query stops after 400 records
findings.surface: GET /api/daily-inputs; long-range pivot data
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: an authenticated consumer requesting a range containing more than 400 saved daily documents receives only the first 400, with no indication that later dates were omitted. The current UI has a separate 93-day cap, so the 400-document cap primarily affects direct API consumers until that frontend limitation is fixed; complete retrieval requires manually splitting the request.
findings.evidence: server.py:230-233 accepts arbitrary start/end ranges but returns find(...).sort('date',1).to_list(400) without pagination, a count or a truncation marker. PivotTab.jsx:55 treats the response as the entire range.
findings.expected: R-039: "for an inclusive start-end range" returns values for all stands; R-059: "a range always includes both its start and end dates"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: capped lists expose pagination or show N of M.
reproduction_steps: Create or retain daily records for more than 400 dates.
Request GET /api/daily-inputs across that entire range.
Compare the returned final date with the requested end date.

findings.title: Blank or duplicate stand names make daily entries indistinguishable — the server accepts invalid names and negative ordering
findings.surface: Settings > Tambah Stand; stands API
findings.observed: Business logic and calculations: the owner can create a whitespace-only stand, a negative order or two identically named stands. Duplicate stand names become indistinguishable in the form and pivot while their independent sales are both added, so correcting or identifying the proper record takes manual investigation.
findings.evidence: StandIn.form_name at server.py:121 only checks min_length=1 so whitespace passes; input_order and wa_order at :127-129 have no lower bounds. :177-180 inserts every stand with a new id without checking form_name; INDEXES :31-37 defines no unique stand-name index.
findings.expected: checklist, Business logic and calculations: "text is trimmed and non-empty" and counts/order have bounds; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "What must be unique is unique in the store through a unique index".
reproduction_steps: Open Settings > Tambah Stand.
Create a stand with only spaces or with a name matching an existing stand, and enter a negative form order.
Open Input Harian and Pivot to inspect the ambiguous records.

findings.title: Clearing a pivot date produces an invalid or empty matrix — date inputs are not validated before matrix construction
findings.surface: Pivot & Export date inputs
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: clearing a range date allows an invalid range into the calculation, yielding an empty or malformed date header and a failed request rather than a field-level explanation while preserving the last valid matrix. Export can later remain available against that invalid range.
findings.evidence: PivotTab.jsx:88,92 directly stores empty date-input values; :52 checks only start > end and :68 passes start to dateRange when start <= end. format.js:32-35 pushes that empty string and calls addDays on it, while pivot.js:10 maps it through ddmm, producing an undefined date label.
findings.expected: checklist, Business logic and calculations: "client and server enforce the same rules, and each error message names the rule the input broke, next to its field"; R-092: invalid date selections must be refused with a visible message and prior matrix retained.
reproduction_steps: Open Pivot & Export with a valid range.
Clear the Dari date input.
Inspect the matrix and error, then try Export Excel.

findings.title: Daily summary still includes a deactivated stand's sales — total calculation uses all master stands
findings.surface: Input Harian running totals after deactivating stands
findings.observed: Business logic and calculations: after deactivating a stand with sales on the selected date, its card disappears but its amount remains in the Input Harian category totals. The owner cannot reconcile the displayed total against the visible active stands.
findings.evidence: InputTab.jsx:16 computes inputStands but :17 passes all stands into computeTotals; wa.js:6-14 sums entries for every stand without checking is_active_input. The summary at InputTab.jsx:34-35 shows those sums.
findings.expected: R-088: the running daily omset "equals the sum of the day's omset values across the active stands".
reproduction_steps: Save omset on WTC.
Deactivate WTC in Settings and return to Input Harian for that day.
Compare Total AMK with the omset on the remaining active cards.

findings.title: Generated dummy days contain no values for newly added cup items — generator only populates three hardcoded WA codes
findings.surface: Settings > Buat 7 Hari; new cup item inputs and Percup
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: after the owner adds a dynamic cup item and generates dummy data, that item's input and pivot cells are empty or zero for every generated day. The example data cannot demonstrate or test the newly configured item.
findings.evidence: generate_dummy reads all items at server.py:253-254, but :266-271 creates cup values exclusively for codes Ck, Cb and Csdng. Any item with another code has no generated entry in any of the seven days.
findings.expected: R-046: "dummy daily rows ... with values for the stands and items"; R-090: added cup items drive the form and pivot.
reproduction_steps: Add an active cup item with a new WA code in Settings.
Press Buat 7 Hari for dates not occupied by real data.
Open an example day and its Percup pivot for the new item.

findings.title: The last keystroke can be lost on an immediate page close — localStorage is written only in a later React effect
findings.surface: Input Harian keystroke draft persistence
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: the newest keystroke exists only in React state until the post-render effect runs. If the page is terminated or crashes in that interval, reopening restores the preceding draft rather than the last input, contrary to the immediate offline-backup promise.
findings.evidence: useDaily.js:99-105 update() only sets React state; :82-87 writes the localStorage draft later in a useEffect after the render. StandCard.jsx:36,50,64 calls update on every input event, with no synchronous localStorage write in the event path.
findings.expected: R-015: "Every keystroke on Input Harian writes the whole selected date's payload to localStorage"; request: "Every keystroke ... MUST immediately save".
reproduction_steps: Edit a sales or SPG field.
Close or terminate the page immediately after the keystroke, before React runs the persistence effect.
Reopen the date and compare the restored draft with the last keystroke.

findings_minor.title: SPG entries change after reload — the client trims names before sending them
findings_minor.surface: Input Harian SPG fields and autosave
findings_minor.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: staff names with leading or trailing spaces are silently rewritten by every save. The input can still display the untrimmed text until reload, after which the saved value differs from what the owner typed.
findings_minor.evidence: useDaily.js:23 maps each SPG string through .trim() before POST; server.py:200-205 and :220 stores exactly the normalized request rather than what was typed.
findings_minor.expected: R-014: "POST /api/daily-input stores spg1, spg2 and spg3 verbatim"; R-074: "stored and returned unchanged".
reproduction_steps: Type an SPG name with a leading or trailing space.
Save and reload the selected date.
Compare the saved field with the originally typed value.

findings_minor.title: The owner cannot find a stand by name — the card list has no search control
findings_minor.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: the owner cannot search for a named stand among the 28 cards and must scroll or use category chips to locate it.
findings_minor.evidence: App.js:53-61 filters stand cards by category only; InputTab.jsx:26-46 renders a summary and those cards without a text input or search handler. The app's source search has no stand-search implementation.
findings_minor.expected: R-087: "A text search over the stand list narrows the cards ... clearing it restores the full list ... a search with no match shows an explicit empty message".
reproduction_steps: Open Input Harian and try to search for a stand by name.

findings_minor.title: Newly saved staff names are not suggested until reload — the autocomplete list is fetched only on initial load
findings_minor.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: an SPG name the owner just saved is not offered in another card during the same session. The owner has to type it again or reload the app to update suggestions.
findings_minor.evidence: App.js:49-51 fetches SPG names only when reloadKey changes; saving at useDaily.js:37-47 does not update reloadKey or refresh the name list. StandCard.jsx:58-64 uses the static spg-names datalist.
findings_minor.expected: R-013: "offer previously entered SPG names as datalist suggestions"; R-014: "distinct SPG names previously saved" are exposed for the screen.
reproduction_steps: Enter and save a new SPG name on one stand.
Focus an SPG input on another stand without reloading.
Look for the new name in the suggestions.

findings_minor.title: The combined daily omset is not shown — the summary displays category totals only
findings_minor.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: the owner can see separate AMK and AMKopi figures but not the requested combined running daily omset, so must add them manually for a full-day sanity check.
findings_minor.evidence: InputTab.jsx:17 computes t.amk and t.amkopi; :33-37 displays those separate values and the filled count, but no sum of both is rendered.
findings_minor.expected: R-088: "Input Harian shows the running total omset for the selected date ... equals the sum ... across the active stands".
reproduction_steps: Enter positive omset for an AMK stand and an AMKopi stand.
Inspect the Input Harian summary for the combined daily total.

findings_minor.title: Some controls and labels remain in English — UI copy is not fully translated into Bahasa Indonesia
findings_minor.surface: Login, bottom navigation, Settings and Pivot
findings_minor.observed: Layout, theme, visuals and UX: the Indonesian interface still presents English labels and terminology including Settings, owner, Password and Edit. The owner sees a mixed-language interface rather than the requested consistent screen language.
findings_minor.evidence: App.js:17 and BottomNav.jsx:7 display Settings; Login.jsx:34 uses owner and :42 Password; SettingsTab.jsx:29 uses Edit; PivotTab.jsx:100,103 displays Export Excel and sheet.
findings_minor.expected: R-004: "Every visible label, button, tab, status pill, empty state and error message on every screen is in Bahasa Indonesia ... with no English left in user-facing copy".
reproduction_steps: Open the login screen, Settings and Pivot & Export.
Read the navigation and control labels.

findings_minor.title: The browser tab shows a generic template product instead of AMK — the HTML shell retains its starter metadata
findings_minor.surface: Browser tab and application document metadata
findings_minor.observed: Layout, theme, visuals and UX: the browser tab and page metadata identify the product as a generic Emergent template, and the document language is marked English. The owner sees the wrong product name in the browser and assistive technology receives the wrong language.
findings_minor.evidence: public/index.html:2 sets lang='en'; :7 sets the description to 'A product of emergent.sh' and :24 sets the browser title to 'Emergent | Fullstack App', rather than the app name.
findings_minor.expected: checklist, Layout, theme, visuals and UX: "The content shown belongs to this product: no template copy ... or another app's name"; R-004 requires Bahasa Indonesia screens.
reproduction_steps: Open the application and inspect its browser tab title.
Inspect the document language with assistive technology or page metadata.

findings_minor.title: Session expiry returns the owner to login without an explanation — the 401 handler discards the server's reason
findings_minor.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: when the owner's token expires, the app abruptly returns to an empty login form without explaining that the session expired. The owner must infer why the page changed and whether the last action completed.
findings_minor.evidence: api.js:16-19 removes the token and dispatches amk-logout for any non-login 401; AuthContext.js:10 handles it only by setUser(false), and Login.jsx:10 initializes an empty error. The backend returns an expiry reason at server.py:72-73, but the UI does not pass it to Login.
findings_minor.expected: R-072: "an expired or invalid token returns them to the login screen with a message rather than an empty form".
reproduction_steps: Sign in and let the token expire.
Perform an action that requests protected data.
Observe the login screen and its missing explanation.

findings_minor.title: The monochrome UI uses extra gray shades outside the requested palette — shared styles hardcode additional colors
findings_minor.surface: Application-wide field, label and header styles
findings_minor.observed: Layout, theme, visuals and UX: fields, labels and status surfaces use additional shades outside the exact requested palette. The UI remains monochrome, so the effect is a visual-spec mismatch rather than a block to entering data.
findings_minor.evidence: App.css:2,6 applies #C7C7CC and #6E6E73; Header.jsx:18,37 uses #F2F2F7 and #6E6E73. These are additional literal colors beyond the specified five-color palette.
findings_minor.expected: R-061: "Every screen uses only the Apple monochrome palette (black #000000, off-black #1D1D1F, white #FFFFFF, gray #F5F5F7, border gray #D2D2D7)".
reproduction_steps: Inspect the login or Input Harian labels, placeholders and draft status styles.
Compare their literal colors against the five requested palette values.

findings_minor.title: Dummy status and cleanup become slower as daily history grows — is_dummy queries have no index
findings_minor.surface: Settings dummy status and clear queries
findings_minor.observed: Performance and resource leaks: Settings checks dummy status and clears dummy days using a field with no serving index. As historical daily records accumulate, these operations must scan the growing daily_inputs collection instead of finding the small dummy subset directly, increasing database work and delaying the Settings action.
findings_minor.evidence: server.py:291 deletes by is_dummy and :297 obtains distinct dates filtered by is_dummy; INDEXES at :31-37 defines only a unique date index for daily_inputs, with no is_dummy index.
findings_minor.expected: checklist, Performance and resource leaks: "each repeated read has an index that serves it"; an index on daily_inputs (is_dummy, date) serves the status lookup and dummy-only deletion.
reproduction_steps: Accumulate a long history of daily records.
Open Settings and request dummy status, or use Hapus Semua Dummy.
Inspect the queries against the configured daily_inputs indexes.
